dataset_name: Vidyashilp University Official Website Knowledge Base
discovery_method: Official homepage navigation plus the university HTML sitemap and indexed official page content
important_usage_note: This is a curated semantic knowledge base of the university website, not a full HTML mirror. Use the individual programme page for the most specific degree and specialisation information. Distinguish major, specialisation track, elective, programme focus and minor. Where the university site has inconsistent lists across pages or sections, state the inconsistency and advise checking the current intake/registration information. Pages marked listed_not_extracted or fetch_failed have no content chunks; do not answer detailed questions from titles alone.

chunking_strategy.description: Exactly 60 page-linked semantic chunks across the university's official homepage, academic programme pages, school pages, centres, research, admissions, news and contact sections. Programme chunks keep degree/major, specialisation tracks, electives and minors separate. Each chunk preserves the originating official URL and page/section identity; missing or inaccessible pages remain marked as not extracted rather than filled from assumptions.

chunks.heading: University overview and programmes
chunks.text: Vidyashilp University is a private university in Bengaluru, Karnataka, established under Karnataka Act No. 20 of 2021. The homepage presents undergraduate programmes across engineering and technology, liberal arts and sciences, business and entrepreneurship, law, and design. Listed programmes include B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering with Data Science or AI/ML specialisations; B.A. Economics and Psychology; B.Des; B.M.S. Digital Business; and integrated B.A. LL.B. and B.M.S. LL.B. programmes.

chunks.heading: Academic leadership and learning areas
chunks.text: The homepage highlights academic leadership across the University's schools and describes learning areas such as Data Science, Design, Psychology, Economics, Digital Business, and Law and Governance. The Data Science area lists topics including machine learning, artificial intelligence, natural language processing, deep learning, algorithms and Internet of Things. These are areas of study, not necessarily individual semester course titles or course codes.

chunks.heading: News, campus and contact overview
chunks.text: The homepage displays university events, public-facing news, campus-life information and application links. The published founding-campus address is No. 125, Bettenahalli, Kundana Hobli, Chapparkallu Road, Bengaluru 562110. The homepage lists 080 6963 0500 for admissions and 089 5118 4990 for other enquiries. Event and application information can change, so use the linked current pages for live details.

chunks.heading: Vidyashilp Education Group and university foundation
chunks.text: The university describes its background through the Vidyashilp Education Group, which began with a single room and 30 students in 1982 and has since developed schools and preschools in Bengaluru. Vidyashilp University is presented as an extension of that education legacy, with an institutional focus on collaboration, responsive learning, service and preparing students for life, work and leadership.

chunks.heading: Vision
chunks.text: The university's stated vision is to provide interdisciplinary learning that contributes to a sustainably inclusive society. It emphasises translating ideas into action and nurturing socially conscious innovators, leaders and change-makers.

chunks.heading: Mission and educational approach
chunks.text: The mission describes developing students' knowledge, skills and values; encouraging teaching, learning, research, innovation and entrepreneurship; supporting interdisciplinary study and real-world partnerships; fostering wellbeing and inclusivity; using technology in experiential learning; and contributing to ecological sustainability and societal challenges.

chunks.page_title: Undergraduate Programmes and Areas of Study
chunks.heading: Undergraduate programme directory
chunks.text: The official undergraduate programme directory lists eight degree offerings: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science and Engineering with Data Science; B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science and Engineering with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning; B.A. (Hons.) / B.A. (Hons. with Research) in Economics; B.A. (Hons.) / B.A. (Hons. with Research) in Psychology; Bachelor of Design (B.Des.); B.M.S. (Hons.) / B.M.S. (Hons. with Research) in Digital Business; B.A., LL.B. (Hons.); and B.M.S., LL.B. (Hons.). Treat degree names, majors, specialisation tracks, electives and minors as separate categories. The current individual programme pages give the detailed options; a programme-directory listing does not itself confirm which choices are open to every batch.

chunks.page_title: Undergraduate Programmes and Areas of Study
chunks.heading: Schools and areas of study
chunks.text: The sitemap groups academic delivery under the School of Engineering and Technology, School of Liberal Arts and Sciences, School of Business and Entrepreneurship, School of Law, and School of Design. Homepage areas of study include Data Science, Design, Psychology, Economics, Digital Business, and Law and Governance. These are broad academic domains and should not be confused with a confirmed course catalogue.

chunks.page_title: B.M.S. (Hons.) / (Hons. with Research) in Digital Business
chunks.heading: Programme overview
chunks.text: The B.M.S. (Hons.) is an interdisciplinary Digital Business degree combining management with technology, economics, psychology, law and data-informed decisions. The page highlights analytical thinking, practical learning, industry engagement, business models and organisational strategy. A B.M.S. (Hons. with Research) pathway is also listed.

chunks.page_title: B.M.S. (Hons.) / (Hons. with Research) in Digital Business
chunks.heading: Programme structure and learning components
chunks.text: The published structure is four years, eight semesters and 164 credits. Listed study areas include critical and design thinking, communication, sustainability, psychology, data visualisation, Python, marketing, accounting, business research, operations, fintech and digital supply chains. This is a programme overview, not a batch-specific semester plan.

chunks.page_title: B.M.S. (Hons.) / (Hons. with Research) in Digital Business
chunks.heading: Digital Business major, BMS specialisation tracks and minors
chunks.text: The B.M.S. (Hons.) / (Hons. with Research) programme identifies Digital Business as its major. Its four named specialisation tracks are Marketing, Finance, Startup Management and HR Management. The research pathway lists Advanced Research Methodology and Dissertation. The detailed programme-structure section lists minors in Data Science, Economics, Design, Law and Technology; the programme overview text elsewhere on the same page lists Data Science, Economics, Design, Law and Psychology. Because the official page gives two different minor lists, do not state that one list is definitively current for every cohort. Ask the student to confirm the admission batch or check the current Digii minor registration list before treating a minor as available.

chunks.page_title: B.M.S. (Hons.) / (Hons. with Research) in Digital Business
chunks.heading: Admissions information
chunks.text: The 2026–27 page lists a four-year full-time programme and a minimum 10+2 score of 50%, irrespective of discipline. Its selection steps include registration, application, a session with the Admissions Programme Head, Dean interaction and personal interview. Verify current fees, deadlines and eligibility on the admissions page.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — Data Science
chunks.heading: Programme overview
chunks.text: The B.Tech. (Hons.) in Computer Science and Engineering with Data Science is a four-year undergraduate honours programme. The current detailed programme page describes Computer Science and Engineering with Data Science as the programme focus/major, and states that students can personalise their path through two specialisation tracks: Applied Deep Learning and Full Stack Development. Track 1 includes Applied Deep Learning, Probabilistic Graph Models, Bayesian Methods in Machine Learning / Generative AI, Natural Language Processing, Multi-Modal Learning and Reinforcement Learning. Track 2 includes Full Stack Development, Backend Systems and API Development, Big Data Analytics, Web Frameworks, Mobile Application Development and Performance Optimization and Testing. Listed minors include Economics, Psychology, Design, Marketing, Finance and Law.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — Data Science
chunks.heading: Programme structure
chunks.text: The public Data Science programme page describes a four-year degree with 180 credits across eight semesters. Its listed study areas include programming in Python, data structures, algorithms, computer organisation, operating systems, networks, databases, data visualisation, artificial intelligence, Internet of Things, statistics, calculus and linear algebra. It also lists advanced data-analysis and research-methods content. Consult batch-specific semester spreadsheets for exact course codes and semester placement.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — Data Science
chunks.heading: Data Science specialisation tracks and interdisciplinary minors
chunks.text: The detailed B.Tech. (Hons.) Data Science page names two specialisation tracks. Track 1 is oriented to applied deep-learning and advanced AI methods: Applied Deep Learning; Probabilistic Graph Models; Bayesian Methods in Machine Learning / Generative AI; Natural Language Processing; Multi-Modal Learning; and Reinforcement Learning. Track 2 is oriented to software and systems development: Full Stack Development; Backend Systems and API Development; Big Data Analytics; Web Frameworks; Mobile Application Development; and Performance Optimization and Testing. The programme lists minors in Economics, Psychology, Design, Marketing, Finance and Law. These are specialisation pathways and interdisciplinary minors, not a list of semester-specific course registrations; the page does not establish which track or minor a particular cohort can select in a given semester.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — AI & Machine Learning
chunks.heading: Programme overview
chunks.text: The B.Tech. (Hons.) in Computer Science and Engineering with Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning is the AI/ML-specialised B.Tech. programme. The official page identifies Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning as the programme specialisation/major focus, within a four-year CSE honours degree. It combines computer science, AI, machine learning, mathematics, data science, ethics and philosophy. The honours core includes Deep Learning, Natural Language Processing, Reinforcement Learning, Image Processing and Computer Vision, and Cloud Computing and AI Model Deployment. The page lists minors in Economics, Marketing, Psychology, Finance, Design and Law. It presents elective choices separately; it does not label those elective subjects as additional named specialisation tracks.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — AI & Machine Learning
chunks.heading: Programme structure and core subjects
chunks.text: The AI/ML programme page describes 180 credits over eight semesters. Its published core areas include data structures, theoretical computer science, algorithms, digital design and computer organisation, object-oriented programming, microprocessors, operating systems, networks, databases, optimisation, machine learning and artificial intelligence. The honours core includes deep learning, natural language processing, reinforcement learning, computer vision and cloud computing with AI model deployment.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — AI & Machine Learning
chunks.heading: Electives and minors
chunks.text: The page describes elective choices such as generative AI, probabilistic graphical models, Bayesian machine learning, multi-modal learning, full-stack development, backend systems and API development, big-data analytics, web frameworks and mobile application development. It lists minors in Economics, Psychology, Design, Marketing, Finance and Law. An elective or minor being listed publicly does not prove it is offered to a particular cohort in a particular semester.

chunks.heading: Economics major, specialisation tracks, minors and research pathway
chunks.text: Vidyashilp University lists the B.A. (Hons.) and B.A. (Hons. with Research) in Economics. Economics is the major. The research pathway is for eligible students and includes a supervised final-semester research project; the programme page says graduates may apply for Ph.D. study after the B.A. The detailed programme-structure section lists seven specialisation choices: Advanced Macroeconomics; Business Economics; Applied Microeconomics; Behavioral Economics; Developmental Economics; Quantitative Techniques; and Open Specialisation. Listed minors are Finance, Data Science, Marketing, Psychology, Law and Design. The programme structure is shown as four years, 165 credits and eight semesters. A separate older BA Economics landing page lists only Behavioural Economics, Business Economics and Developmental Economics; because the official site has more than one version of the Economics page, treat the seven-track list as the detailed programme-page listing and verify actual track availability for the student’s intake.

chunks.heading: Psychology major, specialisation tracks, minors and programme focus
chunks.text: Vidyashilp University lists the B.A. (Hons.) and B.A. (Hons. with Research) in Psychology. The programme focuses on the human mind and behaviour and describes interdisciplinary learning, research foundations, and application across Cognitive Science, Sports Psychology, Data Psychology and employee-engagement programmes. Its named specialisation tracks are Counselling Psychology, Cognitive Psychology and Clinical Psychology. The BA Psychology page lists minors in Data Science, Marketing, Economics, Finance and Design. It describes a four-year programme. Do not treat the broader application areas (Industrial, Organisational, Educational, Sports and Health Psychology) as additional formal specialisation tracks unless another programme source labels them that way.

chunks.heading: Integrated law programme
chunks.text: The B.A., LL.B. (Hons.) is a five-year integrated law programme. The current public programme page describes a curriculum combining liberal-arts disciplines with core legal education, clinical courses and law electives. It highlights focus areas including Intellectual Property Rights (IPR), Technology Law and Arbitration. It also discusses Alternative Dispute Resolution (Arbitration, Mediation, Conciliation and Negotiation) and potential applications of Online Dispute Resolution (ODR), along with advocacy. The page specifies a minimum of 14 discipline courses across at least three subjects/streams, two compulsory English courses, 20 prescribed core legal courses, four compulsory clinical courses and at least six law electives; the honours programme requires at least eight additional law courses. These are published focus areas and curriculum components, not an explicit list titled formal specialisation tracks.

chunks.heading: Integrated business and law programme
chunks.text: The B.M.S., LL.B. (Hons.) is described as a five-year integrated degree combining business management and legal study. The programme page highlights business-related legal areas such as mergers and acquisitions, technology law, intellectual property and international trade law. Its published structure is 205 credits over ten semesters. Admissions eligibility and selection criteria should be checked against the current programme page.

chunks.heading: Programme and career orientation
chunks.text: The programme description presents the B.M.S., LL.B. as distinct from the B.A., LL.B. because it places stronger emphasis on the relationship between business and law. It describes pathways that can include legal practice, corporate legal work, legal analysis, policy, legal technology, research and management-related roles. Public career-pathway lists are indicative programme information, not a guarantee of employment outcomes.

chunks.heading: Research areas
chunks.text: The Ph.D. programme page lists research specialisations spanning Computer Science, Data Science, Mathematics and Statistics, Material Science, Economics, Psychology, Literature, Sociology and Anthropology, Law and Business Studies. Data Science-related areas include artificial intelligence, machine learning, natural language processing, deep learning, multi-modal learning and audio/video analytics. The listed areas may change as research priorities and supervisors are updated.

chunks.heading: Ph.D. admission route
chunks.text: The Ph.D. page describes full-time and part-time options and an admission route involving the Vidyashilp University Ph.D. Entrance Test followed by an interview or viva voce, subject to stated exemptions. The page also publishes intake schedules, application details and eligibility criteria. Because these are intake-specific and regulatory requirements can change, applicants should rely on the current Ph.D. admission notice and official information booklet.

chunks.heading: School overview
chunks.text: The School of Engineering and Technology describes an applied, experiential approach to engineering education. Its public description highlights computational science, data science, machine learning, generative AI and ethical technology, and lists B.Tech. programmes in Data Science and AI/ML. The school page introduces the programmes; exact semester-wise courses and codes should be taken from the relevant batch-specific semester-spread records.

chunks.heading: School overview
chunks.text: The School of Business and Entrepreneurship presents the B.M.S. (Hons.) and B.M.S. (Hons. with Research) programmes. Its public page emphasises personalised academic guidance, industry links, experiential learning, innovation, strategic thinking and entrepreneurship. It also describes exposure to industry mentors, corporate partners and start-up networks, including opportunities to develop and test venture ideas.

chunks.heading: School of Design approach
chunks.text: The School of Design describes learning across design, technology and the humanities. Its themes include climate change, urban needs, human-machine relations, care, ageing, health and sustainability; knowledge sources include scientific, artistic/experimental, cultural/indigenous, ethical and philosophical perspectives. It describes a design process of research, making, reflection, testing, failure and reframing. The School page describes a Design major with choice-based minors in Law, Technology, Management, Psychology or Economics. The dedicated B.Des. programme page separately identifies specialisation tracks in Interactive Design, Film and Animation, Graphic Design, Comics and Sequential Art, Game Design and Extended Reality (AR/VR/XR), with later tracks described as continuations.

chunks.heading: Schools and centres directory
chunks.text: The Schools and Centres directory lists five schools: Engineering and Technology; Liberal Arts and Sciences; Business and Entrepreneurship; Law; and Design. Its centres list includes the Centre for Market Regulations and Governance, Wellness Centre, Centre for Writing, Ethnography Centre, IEEE Women in Engineering and IEEE. The university sitemap additionally lists the Community Engagement Programme and VUCADI.

chunks.page_title: Centre for Market Regulations and Governance (CMRG)
chunks.heading: CMRG purpose and activities
chunks.text: The Centre for Market Regulations and Governance is described as an interdisciplinary research and education initiative spanning law, economics, regulation and governance. It aims to build regulatory literacy, improve governance and contribute to policy reform by connecting academic research with government, industry and other stakeholders. Its focus is on knowledge and practical tools for understanding complex market regulation and institutional decision-making.

chunks.heading: Ethnography Lab purpose
chunks.text: The Ethnography Lab is an initiative linked to the university's research and liberal-arts activity. It provides a platform for faculty, students and external stakeholders to collaborate on ethnographic research and discussion. Its stated objectives include promoting ethnographic methods, community engagement, public knowledge sharing and an intellectual community grounded in fieldwork and conversation.

chunks.heading: Ethnography Lab activities
chunks.text: The lab describes work on urban neighbourhoods, including observation, interviews, oral histories and historical material to understand how places and communities change. It also hosts talks and workshops and contributes to teaching research methods. The public page mentions guided field visits and methods such as walking and sensory ethnography as learning activities for undergraduate students.

chunks.heading: Community engagement focus areas
chunks.text: The Community Engagement Programme describes work across education, health and wellbeing, environment and sustainability, legal support, and sports and culture. Its activities include student volunteering, a legal aid clinic, a community mental-health initiative and a student community-service club. It partners with local Anganwadis and government primary schools, where students support teaching and extracurricular activities.

chunks.heading: Wellness Centre services
chunks.text: The Wellness Centre describes psychological support for students and staff through a qualified counselling psychologist in a confidential setting. The page lists support that may include understanding difficulties, planning responses, improving self-awareness and building resilience. It refers to concerns such as stress, anxiety, depression, academic difficulties, family or relationship concerns, bullying and other personal wellbeing issues. For urgent or emergency concerns, use appropriate emergency services rather than relying only on a webpage.

chunks.heading: Centre for Writing purpose
chunks.text: The Centre for Writing is a faculty-and-student initiative intended to strengthen academic and creative reading, writing and communication within the university. Its activities include workshops, talks and other events; support for university writing courses; a Reading Club; and author lectures. The page describes a longer-term aim of offering individual writing guidance to students.

chunks.page_title: Vidyashilp University Centre for Art, Design and Innovation (VUCADI)
chunks.heading: VUCADI purpose
chunks.text: VUCADI, the Vidyashilp University Centre for Art, Design and Innovation, is described as an interdisciplinary platform for creativity, innovation, social engagement and regenerative thinking. It connects students, faculty, researchers and practitioners across the university's schools and supports projects that bring together business, technology, law, design, humanities and environmental studies.

chunks.page_title: Vidyashilp University Centre for Art, Design and Innovation (VUCADI)
chunks.heading: VUCADI programmes and approach
chunks.text: The centre describes workshops, residencies, public interventions, research projects and collaborative initiatives as ways to connect creative practice with social and environmental change. Its Slow North initiative documents North Bengaluru's changing landscapes, communities, stories and cultural practices through publications, interviews, essays, visual documentation, mapping and public conversations.

chunks.heading: International partnerships
chunks.text: The Office of Global Initiatives describes work to build an international academic ecosystem through institutional partnerships, faculty exchanges and student mobility. The website lists partnerships or initiatives involving the University of Wisconsin–Madison, Babson College, Illinois Institute of Technology, IE University, University of Applied Arts Vienna, F+F School of Design, Japan-COIL Association, Study Japan Initiative and Nordic Centre in India. Programme formats and availability can change by intake.

chunks.heading: Global opportunities and activities
chunks.text: The page presents international summer schools, research opportunities, mobility programmes, visiting faculty and collaborative projects as ways for students and faculty to gain international exposure. It also highlights thought-leadership events and cross-institutional initiatives. Specific eligibility, scholarship availability, dates and seat limits must be checked on the current programme announcement.

chunks.heading: Vidyashilp Research Centre purpose
chunks.text: The Vidyashilp Research Centre (VRC) is described as supporting interdisciplinary and interconnected research, innovation and problem-solving. It works with the university's schools and centres and seeks to connect academia, business, industry and local communities. Its objectives include developing research culture, promoting interdisciplinary projects, pursuing collaborative research and disseminating findings through reports and publications.

chunks.heading: Research support and focus areas
chunks.text: The VRC page describes support such as research fellowships, adjunct or visiting expertise, seed grants and access to available research infrastructure. Listed focus areas include social sciences and liberal arts, statistics and mathematics as foundations for data science, digital-economy research in economics, technology-enabled teaching and learning, and design studies oriented toward the circular economy. The centre is accountable to the university's Research and Innovation Council.

chunks.heading: Events page and upcoming programme
chunks.text: The university Events page separates upcoming and past events. At the time captured, it highlighted an Ethnography Symposium scheduled for 12–13 November 2026 and VU Intersect 2026, a business-planning and panel event for undergraduate students held on 30 October 2026. The page also listed a CMRG workshop on regulatory impact assessments and public consultations scheduled for 8–9 May 2026. Dates and event status must be refreshed before use.

chunks.heading: Media and university news
chunks.text: The Media page collects news coverage, commentary and expert contributions associated with Vidyashilp University and its faculty. Recent items shown during capture included a September 2026 article by Prof. Chandan Gowda, a June 2026 story about the School of Design, and several 2026 media features on social media, mental health, phone addiction, parenting and higher education. This page is dynamic; use the page URL for the latest list and article dates.

chunks.heading: How to apply
chunks.text: The Admissions page explains that selection criteria depend on the programme chosen and links to individual programme requirements. Its described application journey includes starting an application, registering details, completing the application and any programme-specific assessment or selection rounds, attending faculty interactions or interviews where required, and receiving the university's decision by email. Applicants should follow the deadlines and instructions shown for their intake.

chunks.heading: Programme-specific selection and enquiries
chunks.text: The admissions website lists undergraduate choices including B.Tech Data Science, BMS Digital Business, Economics, Psychology, Design and integrated law programmes. It states that selection criteria differ by programme. Students who miss selection-round registration are advised to contact the university enquiry/admissions team; late applications may be considered in some circumstances but are not guaranteed. Always verify deadlines and eligibility on the current intake page.

chunks.heading: Scholarship categories
chunks.text: The scholarship page describes merit-based, need-based and talent-based support. Named categories include the P. Dayananda Pai Scholarship, SAT/Dean's Honours Scholarship, scholarships for talent in sports and creative pursuits, and categories for students from specified family or social circumstances. The page says each scholarship has eligibility rules and a predetermined fee-waiver percentage; applicants can express interest and apply online.

chunks.heading: Scholarship application conditions
chunks.text: The scholarship page states that a student cannot apply for more than one scholarship and that the scholarship committee's decision is final. It distinguishes support offered at admission from other award categories. Scholarship amounts, percentages, criteria and application windows should be checked with the current official scholarship notice rather than inferred from older pages or third-party descriptions.

chunks.heading: Virtual coffee chat
chunks.text: The university offers a 20-minute virtual coffee chat with its counselling team. The page presents it as an opportunity for prospective students and families to discuss programme offerings and the university's admissions approach. Booking requires selecting an academic year, date and time slot and entering the requested contact and school details. Availability and booking rules are displayed on the current booking form.

chunks.heading: Campus address and general contact details
chunks.text: The Contact page lists Vidyashilp University's founding campus at No. 125, Bettenahalli, Kundana Hobli, Chapparkallu Road, Bengaluru 562110. It provides a general-enquiry form and separates reception contacts from admissions contacts. The page lists reception at 089 5118 4990 and admissions at admission@vidyashilp.edu.in / 080 6963 0500. Use the contact page for any updated email or phone details.

chunks.heading: Contact categories
chunks.text: The contact page lists separate contact routes for reception and admissions and also includes a fee-payment email address, vureceivable@vidyashilp.edu.in. The form asks for the user's category, name, email, phone number and message. For admission-specific questions, use the admissions contact; for other enquiries, use reception or the general form. Contact information can change and should be checked on the live page.

chunks.heading: Advisory board and governance contributors
chunks.text: The Advisory Board page lists advisors to the Chancellor and members or former members associated with university governance bodies. Public profiles include academic leaders and former university administrators, legal professionals and industry figures. The sitemap also links to former Board of Management, Academic Council and Research and Innovation Council members. Treat names and positions as website-published profiles that may change.

chunks.heading: Campus facilities and location
chunks.text: The campus page describes the founding campus in Bengaluru and a Central Campus listed as under development. Facilities shown include laboratories, a library, design studios and a university café. The page also highlights student life through sports, clubs, festivals, expeditions and other activities. It describes the campus site as approximately 40 acres; development status and facilities should be reconfirmed on the live page.

chunks.heading: IEEE Women in Engineering student chapter
chunks.text: The IEEE Women in Engineering student chapter at Vidyashilp University is presented as a platform for supporting women in engineering and science. Its stated activities include events, workshops, mentorship and collaborative research. The chapter aims to encourage professional growth, networking, innovation, knowledge sharing, leadership development and gender diversity in STEM.

chunks.page_title: School of Liberal Arts and Sciences
chunks.heading: School overview and learning approach
chunks.text: The School of Liberal Arts and Sciences describes an interdisciplinary approach combining creative learning, quantitative rigour and social inquiry. The page highlights critical thinking, community engagement, experiential and international learning, internships, creative pursuits and student career development. It lists Economics and Psychology undergraduate programmes and features the Ethnography Lab as a research initiative.

chunks.heading: School of Law and legal learning
chunks.text: The School of Law describes five-year integrated undergraduate law programmes and highlights foundational and emerging legal domains. Its public page refers to learning beyond the classroom through moot courts, legal and local bodies, clinics, externships, simulations, competitions and pro bono community service. It also identifies the Legal Clinic and the Centre for Market Regulations and Governance as related activities.

chunks.heading: Booking a campus tour
chunks.text: The campus-tour page invites prospective students and families to schedule a visit and explore the university campus. It states that the university is closed on Sundays and public holidays. The page shows campus images and repeats the founding campus address and admissions contact details. Use the live booking page to check available tour slots and current closure rules.

chunks.text:

These titles and affiliations reflect a Faculty-page snapshot indexed approximately five months before 5 November 2026; faculty roles may have changed. Consult the linked official Faculty directory for current appointments and biographies.

chunks.page_title: Bachelor of Design (B.Des.) — Communication Design emphasis
chunks.heading: B.Des major, specialisation tracks, minors and year-wise structure
chunks.text: Vidyashilp University offers a four-year B.Des. with a communication-design emphasis. The programme identifies Design as the major and describes a studio-led, practice-driven curriculum. In Year 3, Semester 5, the page names Specialisation Track I options: Interactive Design; Film and Animation; Graphic Design; Comics and Sequential Art; Game Design; and Extended Reality (AR/VR/XR). Semester 6 describes Specialisation Track II as a continuation, and Year 4 Semester 7 describes Specialisation Track III. The public page does not name separate option lists for Tracks II and III. The page lists 170 credits over eight semesters. Its programme overview lists minors in Finance, Data Science, Marketing, Psychology, Economics and Law. The broader School of Design page separately describes choice-based minors including Law, Technology, Management, Psychology and Economics; the pages therefore do not give one perfectly consistent minor list. Do not mistake the specialisation-track options for minors.

chunks.page_title: B.Tech. (Hons.) Computer Science & Engineering — Data Science
chunks.heading: Track 1 and Track 2 — detailed specialisation course areas
chunks.text: The dedicated Data Science programme page calls the two options Specialisation Tracks. Track 1: Applied Deep Learning; Probabilistic Graph Models; Bayesian Methods in Machine Learning / Generative AI; Natural Language Processing; Multi-Modal Learning; Reinforcement Learning. Track 2: Full Stack Development; Backend Systems and API Development; Big Data Analytics; Web Frameworks; Mobile Application Development; Performance Optimization and Testing. The page also lists advanced data-science and AI themes including exploratory data analysis, optimisation techniques, machine learning, deep learning, cloud computing and AI model deployment. Keep the track names separate from these honours-core areas and from the listed minors.

chunks.heading: Current Law Honours specialisations
chunks.text: The B.M.S., LL.B. (Hons.) programme page has a section titled “Law Honors Specialization Courses” and explicitly lists the current honours specialisations available as: Public Law; Business and Commercial Law; IPR / Intellectual Property Law; AI & Technology Law; Public Health Law; and General Law.
